tail:
Step 4 propagation is done. Report at `research/frontier-11-alpha-report.md`.

## What I changed

Five prose scaffolds, nothing else — not `plan-spec.json`, `items/`, `library/`, any batch artifact, or a normative doc. No gate reads `plan-*.md` (I checked `tools/`), so this stage carries no gate consequence.

**D9, §CT-2** — all four amendments applied. The `Nat(F,G)` sethood clause is removed from the FS line as an *error*, not a withdrawn preference, and replaced by the Remark formulation; no global counterexample asserted. The size-convention and "full embedding" clauses are grounded in published disk text I opened: `def-functor-category` forms the category only for a small source, `def-embedding-of-categories` makes an embedding faithful *and injective on objects*. §6.3(2) itself is correct — CT-2 misread it — so I left it alone. The `Ring→Set` note keeps its noncommutative-target proof with the trap named.

**§AA-12** — `roots-and-rational-powers` added to `requires` (D2), plus the D1/D12 re-home and rewrite, the bridge item's boundary (coordinate arithmetic only, not the norm), the superseded "no degree here" trap, and the transcendental/D10 ruling. **§RA-33** — the construction of ℂ is cut from DEFS/THMS and `field-extensions-and-the-complex-numbers` added to `requires`; the modulus/`d_2` identification stays at 189. Mirror rows in `plan-complex-analysis-track.md` corrected to match.

**§RA-27b** — D8 recorded, design untouched, flagged for step 10. I put it in the plan file as well as the report deliberately: a future Beta reads the plan file and would otherwise re-apply the design's letter and reintroduce the forbidden B-page dependency.

Also recorded where a plan file explicitly asked for a decision and never got one — AG-1 trap (iv) ("record whichever is chosen"), GT-6 trap (i) — and where GT-6's Erdős–Stone denial is in fact *licensed* by §9.5's own "dedicated extremal page" clause, which a step-6 reader would otherwise read as a violation.

## Two things I'd rather you hear plainly

**A miss of mine.** RA-29's B inventory names the Koch snowflake and the Schwarz lantern. Neither is in batch 2's scaffold *or* its coverage ledger — zero hits for `Koch`, `Schwarz`, `snowflake`, `lantern`. My step-3 review didn't catch it, and I used exactly the "the page design is the naming authority" argument to require the FTC roadmap and Botsko on the sibling page. It's recorded as an open step-6 repair; I have *not* verified my guesses about why each is hard.

**Declined to propagate:** batch 2's two `requires` additions into the RA-39/RA-29 `<-` lines. Those lines are design sketches, not literal requires lists (RA-39's already names RA-11, which the spec doesn't carry), so editing them would imply a mechanical claim they don't make.

## Ready for step 5

`validate-plan --rehomed` OK; **B2 verified closed, not assumed** — batch 1's manifest gate is 54 items / 0 errors; `pre-d1-rewrite` baseline confirmed at 2026-08-11T16:50Z.

The authoring Betas need 14 things beyond their scaffolds, the sharpest being: the four ℂ items stay `status: published` (do **not** draft them — order 189 still lists them); delete `verification.audited` on all four; **none of the four carries a `verification.judge`** — I read all four blocks, so there's nothing to delete there; re-run precheck; and `lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws` must not touch `def-p-norms-on-rn`.

One decision is still yours: from step 5 to the step-10 commit, `depcheck` raises `published-unaudited` — an **error** — on those four. `--pending-audit-ok` exists for this class but its stated sole caller is the audit A4 gate, so using it in a build is a deviation to record, not assume. The window is unavoidable under the rewrite reading; deferring the rewrite would mean the step-7 judges never see the final text.
